ev.byz_x_ransom.title: Ransomed
ev.byz_x_ransom.text: Neighbors, relatives and the church community spent years collecting money to ransom captives. Your name was among the first called: you are free and on your way home.
ev.byz_h_photios.title: Patriarch Photios
ev.byz_h_photios.text: Photios, the most learned layman of the age, has been rushed through every rank of the clergy in a matter of days and made patriarch in place of the deposed Ignatios. Rome refuses to recognize him, and the City argues over whose word counts for more in the Church.
ev.byz_h_photios.note: In 858 Photios, a layman and the greatest scholar of his time, became patriarch after Ignatios was deposed. Pope Nicholas I refused to recognize him and declared him deposed in 863; in 867 a council in Constantinople condemned the pope in turn, the so-called Photian Schism. Basil I removed Photios in 867, but he returned to the patriarchal throne in 877.
ev.byz_h_photios.photios: Back Photios: Rome does not give us orders
ev.byz_h_photios.none: No time for that; there is work to do
ev.byz_h_rus_860.title: The People Called Rus
ev.byz_h_rus_860.text: Two hundred boats of an unknown people called the Rus have sailed into the Bosporus while the emperor and his army are away fighting the Arabs. The suburbs are burning, the island monasteries have been plundered, and Patriarch Photios leads prayers on the walls.
ev.byz_h_rus_860.note: On 18 June 860 a Rus fleet of about 200 ships suddenly attacked the outskirts of Constantinople while Michael III was campaigning against the Arabs. The raiders ravaged the suburbs and the Princes' Islands and then withdrew. Photios left two sermons about the attack.
ev.byz_h_rus_860.save: Save your belongings in the suburbs
ev.byz_h_rus_860.save.success: You got your most precious things inside the walls in time.
ev.byz_h_rus_860.save.failure: The boats arrived first. You barely escaped with your life.
ev.byz_h_rus_860.walls: Shelter behind the walls and pray
ev.byz_h_slavic_mission.title: An Alphabet for the Slavs
ev.byz_h_slavic_mission.text: Two natives of Thessalonica, the scholar Constantine and Methodios, are setting out for distant Moravia to preach to the Slavs in their own tongue. Constantine has invented a new alphabet for the purpose. At the harbor people say the local Slavs understand their speech already.
ev.byz_h_slavic_mission.note: In 862–863, at the request of Prince Rastislav of Moravia, Michael III sent the brothers Constantine (Cyril as a monk) and Methodios, natives of Thessalonica who knew the Slavic language, to Moravia. Constantine created the Glagolitic alphabet; the Cyrillic script later developed from it in Bulgaria.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.title: Saracens in the Harbor
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.text: The fleet of the renegade Leo of Tripoli has burst into the harbor. Saracens are climbing onto the sea walls straight from the masts of their ships. The city that has held off its enemies for centuries is about to fall.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.note: On 29 July 904 an Arab fleet led by Leo of Tripoli, a Greek convert to Islam, took Thessalonica after a three-day siege. The city was sacked and some 22,000 inhabitants carried off; some were later ransomed or exchanged. An eyewitness, the priest John Kaminiates, left a detailed account.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.wall.success: Your stretch of wall held to the end. You survived and sheltered your neighbors.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.wall.failure: The Saracens broke through. Wounded, you were dragged to the ships.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.hide: Hide in the church of Saint Demetrios
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.hide.success: They did not find you. Your house was looted, but you are alive.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_904.hide.failure: They searched the church. You were led away with the other captives.
ev.byz_h_symeon.title: Tsar Symeon
ev.byz_h_symeon.text: Tsar Symeon of Bulgaria, who grew up a hostage in Constantinople and learned his Demosthenes there, is now leading his own army to the walls and demanding the imperial crown.
ev.byz_h_symeon.note: Symeon I (893–927), educated in Constantinople, reached the capital's walls in 913 and extracted a promise that his daughter would marry the young Constantine VII. In 917 he crushed the Byzantines at Achelous, and in 924 he stood before the walls again and met Romanos Lekapenos. He never managed to take the city behind the Theodosian Walls.
ev.byz_h_symeon.militia.success: The Bulgarians withdrew, and you came back alive and full of stories.
ev.byz_h_symeon.militia.failure: You took an arrow in a skirmish beneath the walls.
ev.byz_h_winter_927.title: The Great Winter
ev.byz_h_winter_927.text: A savage winter has come: the ground stayed frozen for months, and after it came crop failure, famine and disease. The poor are selling their land for a handful of bread, and the buyers, of course, are the magnates.
ev.byz_h_winter_927.note: In the winter of 927/928 Byzantium suffered unprecedented cold (the chroniclers say the ground was frozen for 120 days), followed by famine and plague. Peasants sold their land en masse to the "powerful", the dynatoi. In 934 Romanos I Lekapenos issued a law forbidding the powerful to buy up peasant land.
ev.byz_h_winter_927.sell: Sell some land and goods for bread
ev.byz_h_igor_941.title: The Sea on Fire
ev.byz_h_igor_941.text: Prince Igor of the Rus has brought a huge fleet to the Bosporus. Against it sailed just fifteen old ships hastily fitted with Greek-fire siphons, and the sea caught fire. The surviving boats went off to plunder the coasts of Bithynia.
ev.byz_h_igor_941.note: In June 941 the fleet of Prince Igor of Kiev attacked the coast near Constantinople. The protovestiarios Theophanes, with fifteen hastily assembled ships fitted with siphons, burned much of the fleet with Greek fire. The surviving Rus raided the coasts of Bithynia and Paphlagonia for several more months.
ev.byz_h_crete_961.title: Crete Is Ours Again
ev.byz_h_crete_961.text: Nikephoros Phokas has taken Chandax after a winter siege. Crete, a pirates' nest for a century and a half, is Roman again, and loot and prisoners are being shipped to the City. The Aegean can be sailed without fear at last.
ev.byz_h_crete_961.note: On 7 March 961 the general Nikephoros Phokas took Chandax (modern Heraklion), capital of the Emirate of Crete, which had existed since the 820s, after a siege of many months. The end of the emirate sharply reduced Arab raids on the Aegean coasts.
ev.byz_h_vladimir_988.title: The Baptism of the Rus
ev.byz_h_vladimir_988.text: The purple-born princess Anna is being given in marriage to Vladimir, prince of the Rus; in return he will be baptized and baptize his people. Meanwhile six thousand red-bearded Varangians have arrived in the City to help Emperor Basil against the rebels.
ev.byz_h_vladimir_988.note: In 988 Basil II, hard pressed by the revolt of Bardas Phokas, received a force of 6,000 warriors from Prince Vladimir of Kiev, which became the core of the Varangian Guard. The price of the alliance was Vladimir's marriage to the emperor's sister Anna and his baptism; the Rus followed their prince into Christianity. The exact sequence of events is debated.
ev.byz_h_kleidion_1014.title: Kleidion
ev.byz_h_kleidion_1014.text: Emperor Basil has trapped the Bulgarian army in the Kleidion pass. They say thousands of prisoners were blinded and sent back to Tsar Samuel, one sighted man left for every hundred, and the old tsar died at the sight of them.
ev.byz_h_kleidion_1014.note: On 29 July 1014 Basil II defeated Tsar Samuel's army at Kleidion. According to John Skylitzes, some 15,000 prisoners were blinded, with a one-eyed guide left for every hundred; Samuel died on 6 October. The numbers are probably exaggerated. By 1018 Bulgaria had been annexed, and Basil later earned the name Bulgar-slayer.
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.title: The Emperor Winters in Trebizond
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.text: The old emperor Basil and his army have taken up winter quarters in Trebizond after a campaign into Georgia. The town is packed with soldiers, the price of bread and wine has shot up, and envoys from all over the Caucasus are sailing into the harbor.
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.note: In the winter of 1021/1022 Basil II wintered with his army in Trebizond after campaigning against King George I of Georgia. There he received envoys and the testament of the Armenian king John-Smbat, who bequeathed Ani to the empire after his death.
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.sell.success: The soldiers paid generously; the emperor had brought their wages.
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.sell.failure: The soldiers took your goods "on credit" and marched off in spring.
ev.byz_h_basil_winter_1021.hide: Hide the wine and grain from the billeted troops
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.title: "We Want Zoe!"
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.text: The new emperor Michael the Caulker has packed the rightful empress Zoe, niece of Basil the Bulgar-slayer, off to a convent. The City has exploded: crowds storm the palace shouting "We want Zoe!", and the houses of the Caulker's relatives are burning.
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.note: In April 1042 Michael V the Caulker tried to get rid of Empress Zoe, heiress of the Macedonian dynasty. The people of Constantinople rose and overthrew him within two days; Michael was blinded, and Zoe and her sister Theodora ruled jointly. The eyewitness Michael Psellos described the events.
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.storm: March on the palace with everyone
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.storm.success: You were in the crowd when Zoe was brought out onto the balcony. The City rejoiced.
ev.byz_h_zoe_1042.storm.failure: The Varangians at the palace gates met the crowd with axes. You were wounded.
ev.byz_h_schism_1054.title: A Bull on the Altar
ev.byz_h_schism_1054.text: Legates from Rome led by Cardinal Humbert have laid a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Keroularios on the altar of Hagia Sophia. The patriarch has anathematized the legates in return. The people are on the patriarch's side.
ev.byz_h_schism_1054.note: On 16 July 1054 papal legates led by Cardinal Humbert placed a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Keroularios on the altar of Hagia Sophia; the patriarch and synod answered by anathematizing the legates. Contemporaries did not see this as a final break, but 1054 later came to be regarded as the date of the Great Schism.
ev.byz_h_schism_1054.shrug: They will make up; it's happened before
ev.byz_h_manzikert.title: Manzikert
ev.byz_h_manzikert.text: Terrible news from the east: the army has been beaten at Manzikert, and Emperor Romanos Diogenes is a prisoner of Sultan Alp Arslan. While the capital squabbles over power, Turkish bands are spreading across Anatolia.
ev.byz_h_manzikert.note: On 26 August 1071 the army of Romanos IV Diogenes was defeated by the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan at Manzikert, and the emperor was captured. The losses were not catastrophic, but the civil strife that followed in Constantinople opened Anatolia to the Turks: within ten years they reached Nicaea.
ev.byz_h_manzikert.fortify: Lay in bread and mend the walls
ev.byz_h_nicaea_seljuk.title: An Emir in Nicaea
ev.byz_h_nicaea_seljuk.text: Nicaea is in Turkish hands: the emir Suleiman has made it his capital. The churches still stand and trade goes on, but taxes now go to the emir, and his warriors are moving into the city with their families.
ev.byz_h_nicaea_seljuk.note: Around 1081 (sources vary between 1075 and 1081) the Seljuk emir Suleiman ibn Qutulmish occupied Nicaea and made it the capital of his domain, barely a hundred kilometers from Constantinople. In 1097, after a siege by the First Crusade, the city was returned to the empire.
ev.byz_h_nicaea_seljuk.stay: Stay and live under the new masters
ev.byz_h_nicaea_seljuk.flee: Leave for Roman lands across the Bosporus
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.title: Franks with Crosses
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.text: Thousands of Franks with crosses sewn on their cloaks are marching through the empire to free the Holy Sepulchre. First came Peter the Hermit's ragged crowd, now the knights with their horses and baggage trains. The emperor feeds them and demands their oath, and the merchants cannot decide whether to rejoice or hide their goods.
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.text.nicaea: A huge army of Frankish crusaders is camped before Nicaea. After seven weeks of siege the city surrendered, not to them but to Emperor Alexios's men. The Latins are furious at being cheated of their plunder.
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.note: The First Crusade (1096–1099): in summer 1096 the bands of Peter the Hermit reached Constantinople, followed in 1096–1097 by the armies of the knights. Alexios I demanded that their leaders swear an oath for the lands they would reconquer. On 19 June 1097 Nicaea, besieged by the crusaders, surrendered to a Byzantine detachment.
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.trade.success: The Franks paid in silver without haggling.
ev.byz_h_first_crusade.trade.failure: The knights took the goods and forgot to pay.
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.title: The Massacre of the Latins
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.text: A mob backing Andronikos Komnenos has burst into the Latin quarter. Merchants, monks and women are being killed and robbed, and the Latin ships are fleeing the Golden Horn. Smoke hangs over the city.
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.note: In April 1182, as Andronikos Komnenos approached the capital, crowds of townspeople and soldiers massacred the Latin quarter of Constantinople. Thousands died, mostly Genoese and Pisans; some survivors were sold into slavery. The memory of the massacre embittered the Latins and played its part in 1204.
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.shelter: Hide your Latin neighbors in your house
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.shelter.success: You hid them in your cellar for three days, then led them to a boat by night.
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.shelter.failure: The mob found out and wrecked your house.
ev.byz_h_latin_massacre.stay: Bar the doors and wait it out
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1185.title: Normans in Thessalonica
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1185.text: The Normans of Sicily have taken Thessalonica. The city is being looted, their horses are stabled in the churches, and Archbishop Eustathios goes to the Norman counts to plead for the townspeople.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1185.note: On 24 August 1185 the army of King William II of Sicily took Thessalonica. The city was brutally sacked; the invaders held it for several months until they were defeated on the Strymon in November. Archbishop Eustathios of Thessalonica described the events.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1185.hide.success: They left you alone, though the house was stripped.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1185.hide.failure: The soldiers found your hiding place and beat you.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.title: The City Has Fallen
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.text: The crusaders and Venetians, who came to put their own man on the throne, have stormed the City. For three days they loot houses, churches and Hagia Sophia, melt down the bronze statues and cart off the bronze horses from the Hippodrome.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.note: On 13 April 1204 the men of the Fourth Crusade, who had come in 1203 to back the pretender Alexios IV, stormed and sacked Constantinople. The plundering lasted three days; vast quantities of relics and treasure were carried off to the West, including the bronze horses of the Hippodrome, taken to Venice. The Latin Empire was founded. Niketas Choniates left a detailed account.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.hide.success: The looters passed your door by. Almost everything survived.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.hide.failure: The house was picked clean, and you were wounded.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.flee: Flee the City with what you have
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.bribe.success: A Frankish knight took your silver and posted his servant at your door.
ev.byz_h_sack_1204.bribe.failure: One band took the silver; another came right after.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1204.title: An Emperor of Our Own
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1204.text: Alexios and David Komnenos, descendants of Emperor Andronikos, have entered Trebizond with a Georgian army. Alexios has been proclaimed emperor of the Romans: Trebizond now has a basileus of its own, while terrible news arrives from Constantinople.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1204.note: In April 1204, almost at the same time as Constantinople fell, Alexios and David Komnenos, grandsons of Andronikos I, seized Trebizond with the help of Queen Tamar of Georgia. Thus arose the Empire of Trebizond, which lasted until 1461.
ev.byz_h_laskaris.title: Nicaea, the Capital
ev.byz_h_laskaris.text: In Nicaea the patriarch has crowned Theodore Laskaris emperor. Noble families, monks and officials are fleeing here from Constantinople: as long as the City is in Latin hands, the capital of the Romans is here.
ev.byz_h_laskaris.note: After the fall of Constantinople Theodore I Laskaris established himself in Bithynia; in 1208 a patriarch elected at Nicaea crowned him emperor. The Empire of Nicaea became the main center of Roman statehood and recovered Constantinople in 1261.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1224.title: The Latins Leave
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1224.text: Theodore Komnenos Doukas, ruler of Epirus, has taken Thessalonica and driven out the Latins. The city is Greek again, and Theodore, they say, intends to be crowned emperor.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1224.note: After 1204 Thessalonica became the capital of the Latin kingdom of Boniface of Montferrat. In late 1224 it was taken by Theodore Komnenos Doukas of Epirus, who was soon crowned emperor; in 1246 the city passed to the Empire of Nicaea.
ev.byz_h_vatatzes.title: The Egg Crown
ev.byz_h_vatatzes.text: Emperor John Vatatzes wants the realm to live off its own: chickens, horses and cattle are raised on the imperial estates, and with the money from selling eggs, they say, the empress got a new crown, the "egg crown". Foreign silks are frowned upon: wear what is made at home.
ev.byz_h_vatatzes.note: John III Doukas Vatatzes (1222–1254) promoted the economic self-sufficiency of the Empire of Nicaea: according to the historian Nikephoros Gregoras, he paid for an "egg crown" for his wife from the sale of eggs from the imperial estates and forbade his subjects to buy foreign cloth. Vatatzes was later venerated as a saint.
ev.byz_h_kose_dag.title: Tribute to the Great Khan
ev.byz_h_kose_dag.text: The Mongols have crushed the Seljuks at Köse Dağ. The emperor of Trebizond hurries to declare himself a tributary of the Great Khan, but the roads to Tabriz are open now, and the caravans will come through the city.
ev.byz_h_kose_dag.note: On 26 June 1243 the Mongols under Baiju defeated the Sultanate of Rum at Köse Dağ. The Empire of Trebizond, which had fought on the Seljuk side, accepted Mongol overlordship and paid tribute; but trade with Mongol Tabriz made Trebizond one of the richest ports on the Black Sea.
ev.byz_h_recovery_1261.title: The City Is Ours Again
ev.byz_h_recovery_1261.text: A detachment under the Nicaean general Alexios Strategopoulos slipped into Constantinople by night while the Latin fleet was away. The Latin emperor fled, and on August 15th Michael Palaiologos entered the City on foot through the Golden Gate, walking behind the icon of the Hodegetria.
ev.byz_h_recovery_1261.note: On 25 July 1261 a small force under the Nicaean commander Alexios Strategopoulos took Constantinople while the Latin garrison and fleet were absent. On 15 August Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos made his solemn entry into the city. Nicaea quickly lost its role as capital.
ev.byz_h_lyon_1274.title: The Union of Lyon
ev.byz_h_lyon_1274.text: Emperor Michael's envoys at the council in Lyon have accepted Roman primacy and the Latin creed. The emperor fears another Frankish crusade, while in the City the monks and common people cry betrayal of the faith.
ev.byz_h_lyon_1274.note: At the Second Council of Lyon in 1274 Michael VIII's representatives agreed to union with Rome, hoping to forestall Charles of Anjou's planned attack on Constantinople. The union met fierce resistance from clergy and people and was repudiated after Michael's death in 1282.
ev.byz_h_lyon_1274.union: Support the emperor: peace matters more
ev.byz_h_catalans.title: The Catalan Company
ev.byz_h_catalans.text: The Catalan mercenaries whom the emperor himself hired to fight the Turks are taking revenge on the Romans after the murder of their leader Roger de Flor: they burn villages across Thrace and Macedonia and besiege the monasteries.
ev.byz_h_catalans.note: The Catalan Company led by Roger de Flor was hired by Andronikos II in 1303 to fight the Turks. After Roger was murdered in 1305, the Catalans spent years ravaging Thrace and Macedonia, threatening Thessalonica and Mount Athos, and in 1311 they seized the Duchy of Athens.
ev.byz_h_catalans.defend.success: The Catalans went off in search of easier prey.
ev.byz_h_catalans.defend.failure: The mercenaries were more experienced. You were wounded and the farm burned.
ev.byz_h_nicaea_1331.title: Nicaea Surrenders
ev.byz_h_nicaea_1331.text: The emperor tried to break the siege but was beaten at Pelekanos. Nicaea held out as long as it could and then surrendered to Orhan, who promised the townspeople their lives, their property and freedom to leave.
ev.byz_h_nicaea_1331.note: In 1329 Andronikos III was defeated by the Ottomans at Pelekanos while trying to relieve Nicaea. On 2 March 1331 the city surrendered to Orhan on terms that allowed those who wished to leave. Nicomedia fell in 1337, and the Ottomans became masters of Bithynia.
ev.byz_h_civil_war.title: Civil War
ev.byz_h_civil_war.text: After the death of Andronikos III, the regents of the child John Palaiologos and the grand domestic John Kantakouzenos are fighting over power. Both sides call in Serbs and Turks, who ravage Thrace.
ev.byz_h_civil_war.note: The civil war of 1341–1347 between the regency (Anna of Savoy, Patriarch John Kalekas, Alexios Apokaukos) and John Kantakouzenos devastated the empire. Both sides relied on Serbian and Turkish allies; in 1347 Kantakouzenos entered Constantinople and became Emperor John VI. It had been preceded by the war between Andronikos II and his grandson (1321–1328).
ev.byz_h_zealots.title: The Zealots
ev.byz_h_zealots.text: The Zealots have seized power in Thessalonica: they have driven out Kantakouzenos's supporters, loot the houses of the rich and govern the city in the name of the people.
ev.byz_h_zealots.note: In 1342 power in Thessalonica was seized by the Zealots, an anti-aristocratic movement that supported the regency against Kantakouzenos. They expelled and plundered the nobles and ruled the city until 1349/1350, when Thessalonica came under John VI.
ev.byz_h_zealots.archons.success: You saved several families, and nobody informed on you.
ev.byz_h_zealots.archons.failure: The Zealots found out. Your house was ransacked.
ev.byz_h_black_death.title: The Black Death
ev.byz_h_black_death.text: The plague has come with the ships from Kaffa. People are carried off in two or three days, by swellings and a bloody cough. The gravediggers cannot keep up, and churches hold funerals for a dozen at a time.
ev.byz_h_black_death.note: The plague, the "Black Death", reached Constantinople in summer 1347 on ships from Kaffa; the same year it struck Trebizond and other ports. Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos, who lost his son Andronikos to it, left a description of the disease. The epidemic killed a large part of the population and returned many times afterward.
ev.byz_h_black_death.flee.success: You waited out the plague far from the city.
ev.byz_h_black_death.flee.failure: The sickness caught up with you even in the village.
ev.byz_h_black_death.nurse.success: The plague passed you over. Many owe you their lives.
ev.byz_h_black_death.nurse.failure: You caught it from the people you were nursing.
ev.byz_h_black_death.lock.success: You stayed shut in until autumn and survived.
ev.byz_h_black_death.lock.failure: The plague got in even behind a locked door.
ev.byz_h_gallipoli.title: Gallipoli
ev.byz_h_gallipoli.text: An earthquake has brought down the walls of Gallipoli, and its people have fled. The Turks of Suleiman Pasha, Orhan's heir, promptly occupied the town and brought their families. The Ottomans now stand on the European shore.
ev.byz_h_gallipoli.note: On 2 March 1354 an earthquake destroyed the walls of Gallipoli on the Dardanelles. The Ottomans under Suleiman Pasha occupied and settled the town, gaining a permanent foothold in Europe. From there began the conquest of Thrace and the Balkans.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.title: Strife in Trebizond
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.text: Emperors come and go one after another, the great families butcher each other in the streets, and the Genoese, in a quarrel over customs dues, set the suburbs on fire. Nobody knows who will rule tomorrow.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.note: In 1340–1349 the Empire of Trebizond went through dynastic turmoil: several rulers followed one another in a few years amid fighting between noble factions. In 1348–1349 the empire also fought the Genoese over their trading privileges. Order was restored by Alexios III (1349–1390).
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.side.success: Your faction won, and you were remembered when favors were handed out.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.side.failure: Your faction lost. You had to buy your way out.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_strife.aside: Wait it out on the sidelines
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1387.title: The Gates Are Opened
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1387.text: After a four-year siege Thessalonica has opened its gates to the Ottomans. Because the city surrendered, it was not sacked; the churches are left to the townspeople, but taxes now go to the sultan.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1387.note: The Ottoman siege of Thessalonica lasted from 1383; in April 1387 the citizens surrendered on honorable terms. In 1403, after Bayezid's defeat at Ankara, the city was returned to Byzantium under the Treaty of Gallipoli.
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.title: Bayezid's Siege
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.text: Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt has blockaded the City by land. Bread gets dearer every month, people lower themselves from the walls on ropes and give themselves up to the Turks just to eat. Emperor Manuel has gone west to beg for help.
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.note: From 1394 Bayezid I kept Constantinople under blockade. In 1399–1403 Manuel II travelled to Italy, France and England seeking help. The city was saved by Timur's defeat of Bayezid at Ankara on 28 July 1402.
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.trade: Trade secretly with the Turks outside the walls
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.trade.success: A few night trips, and there is bread and silver in the house again.
ev.byz_h_bayezid_siege.trade.failure: A patrol caught you, whether ours or theirs you never knew. You barely got away alive.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.title: The Assault
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.text: Sultan Murad has taken Thessalonica by storm. For three days the city is looted, and thousands of its people are led away as captives. The church of the Virgin Acheiropoietos is already being turned into a mosque.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.note: On 29 March 1430 the troops of Murad II stormed Thessalonica, held by Venice since 1423. The city was sacked and about 7,000 inhabitants were enslaved; later the sultan allowed some who were ransomed to return. The church of the Acheiropoietos became a mosque.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.hide.success: They did not find you. You are alive, though the house is empty.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.hide.failure: They found you and led you away with your neighbors.
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.ships: Fight your way to the Venetian ships
ev.byz_h_thessalonica_1430.ships.failure: The harbor was already blocked. You were seized at the quay.
ev.byz_h_florence.title: The Union of Florence
ev.byz_h_florence.text: Emperor John VIII has returned from Italy: union with Rome was signed in Florence in exchange for promised help against the Turks. The City will not accept it: monks urge people to shun churches where the unionists serve, while others quietly wait for the crusaders.
ev.byz_h_florence.note: The Council of Ferrara-Florence proclaimed the union of the Catholic and Orthodox churches on 6 July 1439. John VIII, who signed it, hoped for Western help. Most clergy and people, led by Mark of Ephesus, rejected the union; it was officially proclaimed in Hagia Sophia only in December 1452.
ev.byz_h_florence.union: Accept the union: without the West we cannot hold
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.title: The 29th of May
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.text: For fifty days the Turkish cannon pounded the Theodosian Walls. At dawn on May 29th the Janissaries broke into the City. The last emperor, Constantine, fell at the gates, and crowds in Hagia Sophia wait for the angel who, the prophecy says, will save the City.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.note: The siege of Constantinople by Mehmed II lasted from 6 April to 29 May 1453. Huge cannon breached the Theodosian Walls, and at dawn on 29 May the Ottomans broke into the city. Constantine XI Palaiologos died fighting. The city was plundered for three days; many inhabitants were enslaved, some later ransomed. Hagia Sophia became a mosque, and Constantinople the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.ships: Fight through to the harbor and the Latin ships
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.ships.success: A Genoese galley cast off with you aboard. The City burned behind the stern.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.ships.failure: There was a crush at the harbor and the ships had gone. You were seized.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.sophia.success: You were let go when the sultan rode into the church and forbade the slaughter.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.sophia.failure: The doors were broken down. The angel did not come.
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.hide: Hide in a cellar and wait
ev.byz_h_fall_1453.hide.success: You came out on the third day. The City was already a different place.
ev.byz_h_gennadios.title: A Patriarch under the Sultan
ev.byz_h_gennadios.text: Sultan Mehmed himself handed the staff of office to the new patriarch, the learned monk Gennadios Scholarios. The Orthodox keep their faith, their own courts for family matters and a few churches, and the sultan is resettling people from all over his realm in the emptied City.
ev.byz_h_gennadios.note: On 6 January 1454 Mehmed II installed Gennadios II Scholarios, an opponent of the union, as patriarch and granted the Orthodox community self-government in matters of faith and family law. The sultan carried out mass resettlements to his new capital of Greeks, Armenians, Jews and Muslims.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1461.title: The Last Realm of the Romans
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1461.text: Sultan Mehmed's fleet and army have reached Trebizond. Emperor David Komnenos has surrendered the city without a fight in exchange for his family's lives. The nobles are being shipped off to Istanbul, and the last realm of the Romans becomes a Turkish province.
ev.byz_h_trebizond_1461.note: In August 1461, after a siege, David Komnenos surrendered Trebizond to Mehmed II. The nobility and part of the population were moved to Istanbul; in 1463 David and his sons were executed. The Empire of Trebizond was the last fragment of Byzantium to fall to the Ottomans.
